matching.notes: Patterns are plain phrases matched as case-insensitive substrings against normalized contract text (collapse whitespace before matching). No regex at this stage.

categories.name: Auto-renewal without adequate notice
categories.description: The agreement rolls over into a new term on its own, and the window to opt out is short or easy to miss. A missed deadline silently locks the customer into another full term at the counterparty's pricing.
patterns: thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current term

categories.name: Unlimited liability
categories.description: One party's exposure is uncapped, or an existing cap is expressly waived. Losses can exceed the total value of the contract, which makes the risk impossible to price or insure against.
patterns: shall be liable for any and all damages
shall not be subject to any cap
aggregate liability shall not be limited

categories.name: Unilateral termination rights
categories.description: Only one party can walk away, or can do so instantly and without cause, while the other is locked in. This removes any leverage the disadvantaged party has and makes long-term planning around the contract unsafe.
patterns: may terminate this agreement at any time, with or without cause
at its sole discretion, terminate this agreement
sole and absolute discretion to terminate
terminate this agreement for convenience at any time without notice
immediately upon written notice, without any liability
shall have no right to terminate

categories.name: Exclusivity clauses
categories.description: The agreement restricts one party from working with anyone else in a given market, category, or territory. This forecloses competitive alternatives and can be a problem if the counterparty underperforms mid-term.
patterns: shall not engage any third party
shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit or engage any competitor

categories.name: Broad indemnification
categories.description: The indemnity sweeps in claims of any kind, including ones caused by the indemnified party's own fault or negligence, rather than being limited to defined third-party claims. It converts a narrow risk allocation into an open-ended guarantee.
patterns: any and all claims of any kind whatsoever
any and all liabilities, losses, damages
arising out of or in any way related to
including claims arising from the negligence of
